design:
D1. Tab kinds are a closed literal union in the UI (`specs`, `files`, `loops`, `spec:<id>`, `file:<path>`, `loop:<id>`); the kind is derived from the id, never stored beside it or built from external input.

D2. Index tabs launch keyed detail tabs; reopening an open tab bumps a reveal counter instead of duplicating it.

D3. The store persists `{version, projects}` in localStorage under one key, per project, with a migration chain; an unknown version is discarded rather than guessed at. Width is not in it: the conversation width preference is global.

D4. Reconciliation drops only `file:` and `spec:` tabs, and only for a kind whose listing has loaded. Index and loop tabs never dangle.

D5. The overlay threshold and the column's minimum both read `minWidthForTabKind`, so they cannot disagree.

D6. File content is allowlisted by membership of the path listing, plus `ProjectWorkspace.resolve_relative` to refuse symlink escapes; no second traversal check.

D7. Attaching a document and reading a document are separate: the attach drives the tab open, never the reverse.

checked: hub/ui/src/__tests__/panelTabsStore.test.ts (keys, open/close rules, persistence, migration, reconcile, restore rules)
hub/ui/src/__tests__/panelShell.test.tsx (one tab at a time, plus menu, launcher, keyboard tablist)
hub/tests/browser/test_panel_shell.py, test_files_tab.py (overlay, document attach vs read, file-replaces-tree, insert)
limits: `panelTabsStore.reconcile` is unit-tested but has no production caller (grep of hub/ui/src outside __tests__), so dangling file and document tabs are not dropped on load today; a missing file's tab shows the 404 sentence instead. The requirement is kept; see report.

lifecycle: Imported from openspec 2026-10-07; overhauled 2026-10-08 against the code at e25e059.
problem: Specification documents, workspace files and loops each need to be read beside the conversation without leaving it. Separate side surfaces with their own rules for opening, closing, width and narrow windows made the right-hand side unpredictable.

requirements.rationale: One surface with one set of rules; an empty shell that reads as a launcher, not a broken grey box.
requirements.statement: The conversation surface SHALL host at most one panel shell beside it, whose strip shows only the tabs currently open and whose body renders the content of exactly one of them. Every open tab SHALL be closable, closing the last one SHALL close the shell, and an open shell with no tab SHALL show a launcher card for every index tab it can open, each with a one-line description and, where the caller supplies one, a count of live items.

requirements.rationale: Offering an already-open tab would read as "open another" when it cannot.
requirements.statement: The shell SHALL offer a plus menu listing only the index tabs (Specs, Files, Changes, Terminal, Watch, Running) that are not already open, and SHALL hide it once all are open. Opening a tab that is already open, from any entry point, SHALL make that tab visible rather than open a second one.

requirements.rationale: Opening the same thing again means "show it to me again", not "give me a copy".
requirements.statement: Selecting an item from an index tab SHALL open a detail tab for that item and make it visible. Selecting an item whose detail tab is already open SHALL make that tab visible and re-reveal the item within it, and MUST NOT open a second tab for the same item.

requirements.rationale: Documents can be renamed by agents; a path-keyed tab would dangle for a document that still exists.
requirements.statement: A detail tab SHALL be keyed by an identifier that survives renaming wherever the item has one: a specification document by its Hub document id (falling back to its path only until the document inventory has loaded, then re-keyed in place without changing which tab is visible), a loop by its loop id, and a file by its workspace-relative path.

requirements.rationale: The file tree is a launcher, and in a narrow column a tab spent on it once used is wasted; the loops and specs indexes are worth keeping in view.
requirements.statement: Opening a file detail tab SHALL close the Files index tab in the same step. Opening a loop or a specification document from its index MUST NOT close that index.

requirements.rationale: Each project has its own working set of documents and files; nothing suggests the operator wants a different width per project.
requirements.statement: Which tabs are open, their order, which is visible and whether the shell is open SHALL be stored in this browser per project and restored when the operator returns to that project, and MUST NOT be shared between projects. The width of the conversation beside the shell SHALL be one value shared across every project and conversation.

requirements.rationale: Persisted tabs point at things that can stop existing; a misread configuration is worse than a lost one, and a listing that has not loaded must not be read as "nothing exists".
requirements.statement: Persisted tab state SHALL carry a version and SHALL be migrated step by step on load when older, and discarded when newer or when no migration step exists. Unreadable or malformed state SHALL be ignored, and duplicate tab ids dropped. A file or document detail tab whose item no longer exists SHALL be dropped, but only once the listing of that kind has loaded. If restoring leaves no tab, the shell SHALL be restored closed; if the visible tab is gone while others survive, a survivor SHALL be made visible.

requirements.rationale: The threshold is derived from the same per-kind minimum the column uses, so the layout and the switch to overlay cannot disagree; the chosen width is clamped, not overwritten, when the window narrows.
requirements.statement: The boundary between the conversation and the shell SHALL be draggable, bounded only by the conversation's minimum width and the visible tab kind's own minimum width. When the available width is below the conversation minimum plus the visible tab's minimum plus the divider, the shell SHALL open as an overlay drawer instead of a column; dismissing the overlay MUST NOT close the open tabs, and a control above the conversation SHALL reopen it.

requirements.rationale: The tree is for finding your way around; search is for when you know the name.
requirements.statement: The Files index tab SHALL present the project's workspace path listing as a navigable tree marking the file currently open, SHALL switch to a ranked flat list of matches while a search is typed (Escape clears it), SHALL state an empty workspace or an empty search rather than show an empty box, and selecting a path SHALL open that file's detail tab.

requirements.rationale: Membership of the listing is the allowlist; the containment check exists only because git lists a symlink by its own path, not its target.
requirements.statement: `GET /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/workspace/file?path=` SHALL serve content only for a path that is byte-for-byte a member of the workspace path listing for that project and whose resolved location lies inside the project's workspace root; any other path, including traversal, ignored files and symlinks pointing outside the workspace, SHALL be answered 404.

requirements.rationale: A silently truncated file is worse than a clear refusal.
requirements.statement: A file up to the Hub's maximum body size SHALL be served in full; a larger file SHALL be refused with 413 and a message stating its size and the bound, checked before any content is read, and MUST NOT be served truncated.

requirements.rationale: Garbled bytes are never useful; an extensionless text file is still text.
requirements.statement: The Hub SHALL classify a file as binary when a NUL byte appears in its first 8,000 bytes and SHALL then return no content; the file tab SHALL state that the file is binary and its size instead of rendering it. Text SHALL be decoded as UTF-8 with replacement and rendered with syntax highlighting, or as Markdown for Markdown files.

requirements.rationale: A mention inserted from either surface is indistinguishable, and an unsafe path would type a second live mention.
requirements.statement: A file detail tab SHALL offer "Insert into composer", which appends to the conversation's composer text exactly the mention the composer's own `@` trigger produces for that path, separated by a space from text already typed. The control SHALL NOT be offered for a path containing an `@` that is neither its first character nor directly after `/`.

The tab strip SHALL follow the tablist pattern with automatic activation: only the visible tab is in the sequential focus order, Left/Right arrows move focus and activation between tabs with wrap-around, Home/End jump to the first and last tab, Enter or Space activates a focused tab, and each tab's close control and the plus menu are reachable and operable by keyboard. A newly visible tab SHALL be scrolled into view in the strip.

requirements.rationale: Tidying the reading pane is not an edit to what the agent is working on.
requirements.statement: Closing a specification document's tab, or opening a document from the Specs index, MUST NOT change which document the conversation has attached; attaching a document SHALL open or reveal its tab, and only the composer's stop-exploring control SHALL detach it (also closing the shell).

requirements.rationale: The operator replaced Loops rather than adding beside it; a stale stored tab must not resurrect the old view or vanish silently.
requirements.statement: The side panel SHALL offer a Running index tab wherever it offered Loops (tab strip, plus menu, empty-state launcher with a count of items that need the operator or are working), and MUST NOT offer Loops any more. A Loops tab persisted from before SHALL be restored as Running, in the same strip position and visibility.

requirements.rationale: A build runs as a loop, and a loop is a job; showing all three layers would triple-count one piece of work.
requirements.statement: Running SHALL list every build of every specification document in the project (whatever drives it, running or ended), every loop that is not a build's, and every scheduled job that is not a loop's, and MUST list each piece of work exactly once.
Running SHALL group items in this order, leaving empty groups out: Needs you, Working now, Between steps, Scheduled, Paused, Finished, Stopped early; each group heading SHALL show its item count.

requirements.rationale: The operator's complaint was that the old tab did not say what needs them.
requirements.statement: An item that has not ended SHALL be in Needs you when its work has an unanswered question or when the Hub would refuse its next firing. Its row SHALL say which, in one sentence (the stall reason as the Hub states it), and offer Answer for a question or Look for a refused firing. Answer SHALL take the operator to where that question can be answered, and Look to the item's own record.

Each row SHALL show the item's name, its kind (Build, Loop or Job), the one time that matters for its group in relative words (started, next, ended or last ran), tasks done out of total where the item has a queue, the amount spent where a build has spent any, and up to two agents each with what they are doing (building, checking, holding, next on, running) and on which task, followed by "and N more" when there are more; where nobody is working it, one status line instead (for a job, its schedule).

Running MUST NOT show raw ids, cron expressions or event names. A schedule the app cannot say in words SHALL read "On its own schedule", and an amount or time SHALL be formatted the way the rest of the app formats it.

Running SHALL offer a Now / Finished / All filter, defaulting to Now (everything that has not ended), with each choice's count shown, and a filter by kind (Everything, Builds, Loops, Jobs) that narrows the list and the counts together; a filter that leaves nothing SHALL say so rather than show an empty box. A summary line above the filters SHALL count items that need the operator, are working, and are waiting.
Selecting a row SHALL open the item: a build opens its specification document in the panel at its builds, a loop opens the loop's detail tab, and a job opens the Jobs page.

Running SHALL reflect a change in a build, loop, job or question (a task taken, a firing started or ended, a question asked or answered) without the operator reloading, as quickly as the panel's other live views do.
Running SHALL render as the mock approved on 2026-11-12 does, in dark and light, at the panel's narrowest width without horizontal scrolling.

With a conversation open, the side panel's Changes tab lists every file the conversation's agent changed on the branch it shows, each with its path, whether it was added, modified, deleted or renamed, and its count of added and removed lines.
Selecting a listed file shows its diff in the panel, without leaving the conversation.

requirements.rationale: Last turn answers 'what did it just do'; since main answers 'what would land'.
requirements.statement: The operator can switch the tab between 'Last turn' (what the agent's most recent finished turn committed) and 'Since main' (everything on the branch that main does not have), and the tab names the branch and the base it compares with.

requirements.rationale: A flow builder's work sits on the task branch; its own branch would look empty.
requirements.statement: When the agent is working a task on a task branch, or its most recent turn was on one, the tab shows that task branch and names the task; otherwise it shows the agent's own branch.

While one of the agent's turns is running, the tab shows a 'working now' line naming the files changed in its checkout but not yet committed; when the turn ends the line goes and those changes appear under Last turn.
When a turn of the agent ends, an open Changes tab shows that turn's changes within 5 seconds, without the operator reloading.
When the agent has changed nothing, the tab says so; when the agent has no checkout of its own, or its branch cannot be read, the tab says which, instead of showing an empty list or an error code.
The tab is offered wherever the Files tab is offered, including when the app is opened from another machine and when the Hub runs in Docker mode.

A change of 200 files, or a single file diff over 5,000 lines, opens the tab within 2 seconds; binary files are listed without a diff body, and a diff too large to show whole says so and shows its start.
From a changed file, the operator can open that file in the Files tab.

requirements.rationale: Two tabs side by side that disagree on which checkout is 'the agent's' would show a diff of one tree and the files of another.
requirements.statement: When the conversation's agent has a checkout of its own, the Files tab offers a switch between that checkout and the project root, and the tab names which one it is showing; the checkout is the one the Changes tab shows for the same conversation (the task checkout when the agent is working or last worked a task, otherwise the agent's own worktree).

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-14: the checkout is where the agent is working, so it is the useful default; a choice made on purpose should stick.
requirements.statement: When the agent has a checkout, the Files tab first opens on it; after the operator switches location, the tab reopens on the location last chosen for that conversation, including after a page reload, while other conversations keep their own choice.

When the agent has no checkout of its own (a read-only agent, or one whose worktree has not been created), the tab offers no switch, shows the project root, and says the agent works in the project directory or has no checkout yet; it never shows an empty tree or an error code for that reason.

With the checkout chosen, the tab lists that checkout's files under the same rules as the project root (tracked files plus untracked files git does not ignore), as a collapsible tree with a find box, including a file the agent created and has not committed.

requirements.rationale: The worktree read must not become a way round the guards the root read already has.
requirements.statement: Opening a file reads it from the location it was listed in; a request naming a path the chosen location does not list, a path escaping it through a link, or another project's or another agent's checkout is refused, and files over 1 MB and binary files are handled as the project-root preview handles them today.

In the checkout, every file the agent changed on its branch since main is marked added, modified or deleted (a deleted file still listed, struck through), and a Changed only switch narrows the tree to those files; the set equals the Changes tab's Since main list for the same conversation.

An opened code file shows syntax-highlighted and an opened Markdown file shows rendered, legibly in both the light and dark themes, and the file's tab names its path and whether it came from the checkout or the project root; the same path opened from both locations opens two distinct tabs.
Insert into composer works for a file opened from either location and inserts its path relative to that location.
When a turn of the agent ends, an open Files tab showing its checkout lists any file that turn created, and updates its changed marks, within 5 seconds and without a reload.

requirements.rationale: A shell runs any command as the operator; anyone who could open one from elsewhere owns the computer.
requirements.statement: The Hub opens a shell only for a request from a loopback address made by the signed-in operator; a request from any other address, Docker bridge addresses included, or without the operator's sign-in, is refused and starts no process, and the Terminal tab used from another computer says the terminal opens only on the computer AgentWeave runs on.

requirements.rationale: Browsers let any website open a live connection to localhost; without this, a page the operator merely visits could run commands.
requirements.statement: A request to open or attach to a shell whose origin is not the app's own page is refused and starts no process, even from the Hub's own computer.
A Hub running in Docker mode offers no terminal: the tab says the terminal is not available in Docker mode and the Hub refuses every shell request.

The menu for a new shell lists the shells installed on the Hub's computer and only those: on Windows, whichever of PowerShell 7, Windows PowerShell, Command Prompt and Git Bash are found, and each installed WSL distribution; elsewhere, the operator's login shell and the installed shells the system lists. The operator's last pick is listed first and marked.

A new shell starts in the conversation agent's worktree or the project root, as the operator chose, and its tab shows the shell's name and that directory as the shell names it (a WSL shell's /mnt/<drive>/... path); when the agent has no worktree, the worktree choice is unavailable and says why.

What the operator types reaches the shell and its output appears as it is produced, with colour and cursor movement drawn correctly enough that full-screen programs (an editor, a pager) are usable, and the shell's size follows the panel's size.
A conversation can have up to four open shells at once, each in its own tab with its own directory and shell; asking for a fifth is refused with a message naming the limit and starts no process.

requirements.rationale: A dev server or a long test run should not die because the operator went to answer another agent.
requirements.statement: A conversation's shells keep running while the operator is in another conversation, another tab or has the panel closed; returning shows each shell with the output produced meanwhile, up to its last 5,000 lines.

requirements.rationale: On Windows a shell's children outlive it unless ended with it; an orphaned dev server holds its port.
requirements.statement: Closing a shell, Restart, reloading the page and stopping the Hub each end the shells concerned and every process they started; after a reload no earlier shell is listed and opening the Terminal tab starts one fresh shell. A shell that exits by itself shows that it ended, with its exit code, and offers to open it again.

requirements.rationale: Whatever runs in the shell, and any agent reading its output, must not be handed the Hub's secrets.
requirements.statement: A shell, WSL shells included, has the operator's environment, including PATH, without the variables the Hub itself holds: its database location, its API keys and any agent's run credentials.
The operator can send a selection of a shell's output, or its visible screen when nothing is selected, into the conversation's composer, unsent, marked with the shell's name and directory.

The conversation's agent has a tool that returns, for each open shell of that conversation, its shell name, directory, whether it is still running and up to its last 500 lines of output; it cannot type into, start or end a shell, an agent of another conversation gets none of them, and the Terminal tab says the agent can read its shells.
The conversation side panel offers a Watch tab alongside Specs, Files, Running, Changes and Terminal, opened, closed and remembered like the others (which tabs are open is kept per project).

requirements.rationale: A flow runs the same agent in several conversations, so watching only other agents would miss the case the operator asked for (operator, 2026-11-15).
requirements.statement: The Watch tab's agent menu lists every agent of the current project, including the conversation's own agent, each with its colour and what it is doing now; its conversation menu lists the chosen agent's open conversations, newest activity first.

requirements.rationale: With what is watched kept per project, the main view can arrive at the watched conversation; two copies of one timeline side by side add nothing.
requirements.statement: When the watched conversation is the one shown in the main view, the Watch tab does not draw it a second time: it says the operator is in this conversation and offers the watched agent's other conversations; watching resumes when the main view moves elsewhere.

Choosing an agent opens the conversation it is running now, or its most recently active conversation when it is idle; an agent with no conversation shows that it has none yet rather than an empty timeline.

requirements.rationale: Following keeps the tab live as a flow moves the agent from task to task; a hand pick is a deliberate choice that must not be taken away mid-read.
requirements.statement: While the operator has not picked a conversation by hand, the tab switches to the conversation the watched agent starts running next; once the operator picks one by hand, it stays on that conversation until they choose an agent again.

requirements.rationale: Watch only (roadmap, operator 2026-11-12): two composers side by side make it easy to write to the wrong agent.
requirements.statement: The watched conversation is drawn as the main view draws it (messages, turn output, tool calls) and new output appears as the agent produces it without a reload; the tab offers no way to send a message, answer a question, stop a run or change the queue.

requirements.rationale: Waiting for an answer is the state the operator most needs to see (operator, 2026-11-15).
requirements.statement: The tab says whether the watched agent is working, idle, or waiting for the operator's answer, the last whenever the agent has an unanswered question, and the statement changes when that state does without a reload.

requirements.rationale: The tab's purpose is keeping an eye on one agent while talking to several; it matches the panel's other per-project state (operator, 2026-11-15).
requirements.statement: The watched agent and conversation are kept per project: switching the main view to any other conversation of the project, or reloading the page, leaves the Watch tab showing the same agent and conversation; a remembered conversation that has since been closed falls back to the default conversation of that agent, and a remembered agent that no longer exists leaves the tab asking which agent to watch.
The tab has a control that makes the watched conversation the main view in one click, where the operator can talk to that agent; the conversation they left keeps its unsent draft.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-15: grey text does not say what is happening. Waiting currently looks the same as idle, yet it is the one state that needs the operator.
requirements.statement: The Watch tab's status line shows each state in its own colour with a mark beside it: working in the app's green, waiting for your answer in the app's amber, idle in a muted neutral. The three states cannot be confused with colour alone or with the text alone.

requirements.rationale: Motion is what says 'something is happening now' at a glance; a different rhythm for waiting keeps it from reading as work in progress.
requirements.statement: While the watched agent is working, its mark pulses continuously; while it is waiting for your answer, its mark draws attention with a slower, distinct pulse; idle has no motion. When the state changes, the colour and motion change with it, without a reload.
The agent menu's entries show each agent's state in the same colour as the status line, so the operator can see who is working or waiting before choosing whom to watch.

requirements.rationale: Accessibility, and the app already honours it everywhere else (index.css's prefers-reduced-motion rule).
requirements.statement: With the operating system's reduce-motion setting on, the marks keep their colours but do not pulse.

in_scope: The panel shell, its tab strip, plus menu and empty-state launcher
Per-project tab persistence and its restore rules
The conversation/panel boundary, and the overlay below the combined minimum width
The files index tab, the file detail tab, and the workspace file content endpoint
Inserting a file mention into the composer from a file tab
non_goals: What a specification document tab renders (spec-document-authority, spec-chat-session)
What the loops index and loop tabs show (agent-loops)
The workspace path listing endpoint itself (agent-composer)

summary: One panel shell beside a conversation, showing one tab at a time: the specs, files and loops index tabs and the keyed detail tabs they open (a specification document, a workspace file, a loop). The operator controls the tab strip; tab configuration is remembered per project, the width is one global preference, and one resize/overlay rule applies whatever is shown.
title: Conversation side panel
